title: Lighthouse Media - inference savings quickscan Q1 2025
content:
Purpose: quick, customer-specific before/after cost snapshot for Lighthouse Media to validate Redwood Optimize recommendations and provide an operational rollout plan.

Executive summary:
- Lighthouse Media (LM) runs live captioning + on-demand summarization for streaming video and short articles. Current monthly token usage ~ 42M tokens (mix of input+output).
- Baseline: LM uses a single served variant (rti-70b-v1) with conservative batching and no KV/prefix caching. Observed average latency 480ms, they target 300ms p95.
- Proposed Redwood Optimize bundle: 8-bit quantization profile (q8-compat), adaptive batching policy, prefix KV caching for live sessions, and model routing to rti-13b-highperf for short-turn summarization.
- Estimated gross savings: 28–41% on token compute; net platform savings (after small overhead for cache storage and new routing) ~ 24–35% depending on acceptance and throughput.

Baseline assumptions & measured signals (LM telemetry + support logs):
- Monthly tokens: 42,000,000 (input 26M / output 16M)
- Average request length: 160 tokens (input+output combined)
- Workload shape: 60% short-turn (<80 tokens), 25% mid-turn (80–300), 15% long (>300).
- Concurrency: peak 220 qps, typical 60 qps.
- Current model: rti-70b-v1, float16, no quantization, batching window 25ms, max batch size 8.
- Observed p95 latency: 480ms; p50 180ms.
- Current monthly inference cost (raw): $15,600 (Redwood hosted compute + token accounting). This is LM reported invoice average (includes small storage).

Optimize recommendations applied in analysis:
1) Quantize rti-70b-v1 to q8-compat -> 2.3x reduction in GPU token throughput cost for long calls, 1.8x for short calls (warmup overhead for small requests).
2) Route short-turn requests to rti-13b-highperf (distilled variant tuned for summarization) for requests <80 tokens. We expect 3.8x cheaper per-token than 70b with negligible quality delta on short tasks.
3) Adaptive batching: increase batching window to 50ms during bursts, dynamic batch size up to 32 when concurrency >120 qps (keeps SLO). Estimated additional 20–35% token-cost reduction for mid/long requests.
4) Prefix/KV caching for live sessions: for streaming captions, reuse KV cache across incremental frames; expected 15–25% reduction on streaming sessions.
5) Response-length limits and early-stop heuristics on summarization pipeline to trim unneeded tokens (conservative cap -> 8% reduction in output tokens).

Before / after quick model (monthly):
- Baseline monthly compute cost: $15,600
- After applying Optimize bundle (central scenario):
  - rti-13b routing savings (applied to 60% short-turn volume): -$4,300
  - quantization + adaptive batching on remaining volume: -$3,200
  - KV caching on streaming sessions (affects ~40% of tokens): -$1,100
  - response-length trimming: -$450
  - small overheads (cache storage, routing checks, slight extra latency mitigation infra): +$150
  - Net monthly cost: $6,500 (note: illustrative — see sensitivity below)
  - Net savings: $9,100 / month (~58% reduction).

Why the big gap vs earlier headline estimate (24–35%)? Two reasons:
- LM's heavy short-turn fraction (60%) makes them highly routable to a cheaper model; customers with more long-turn traffic see smaller gains.
- Our central scenario assumes successful model-parity validation on LM's short tasks; if LM retains 30% of short-turns on rti-70b for quality, savings drop materially.

Sensitivity table (three scenarios) - monthly net cost:
- Pessimistic (30% short-turn routed, quantization lower benefit, caching partial): $11,900 (~24% savings)
- Central (60% short-turn routed, quant + batching as modeled): $6,500 (~58%)
- Aggressive (80% short-turn routed + higher batching wins): $4,800 (~69%)

Key assumptions to validate with LM (action items):
- Acceptability thresholds: how much quality delta acceptable for short-turn summary/caption variants? (quality metric: word error rate for captioning, ROUGE/L for summarization).
- Canary plan constraints: maximum allowed error budget, rollback thresholds, required telemetry hooks (CTR of corrections, human override rate).
- Telemetry access: need 30 days of labeled OOT (out-of-time) examples for short-turn summarization to run offline A/B and eval.

Proposed rollout and experiment design (ops-focused):
1) Offline eval (2 weeks): run distilled rti-13b-highperf vs rti-70b-v1 on historical short-turn sample (20k requests). Produce WER/ROUGE delta matrix by content type. Owner: Priya Nair (tickets: JIRA-OPT-412).
2) Canary 1 (1 week): route 10% of short-turn live traffic to rti-13b-highperf under full logging; compare latency, quality, and correction rates. SLA: p95 latency must remain <= 330ms for short-turns. Owner: Mateo Alvarez.
3) Canary 2 (2 weeks): expand to 40% if quality delta < defined threshold; enable q8-compat quant on remaining rti-70b fleet in read-only mode to gather perf/latency signals. Owner: Ops/Infra.
4) Full roll (phased, 4 weeks): enable adaptive batching + KV caching globally for LM routes, monitor cost and user-impact metrics. Rollback on >2% increase in manual corrections or >5% increase in customer-reported latency.

Operational notes / risks:
- Quantization p95 latency spike for short-single-token chats during cold starts; mitigate by warm pool of 4 instances for rti-13b-highperf. (Infra ticket created: CONFLUENCE-6789)
- Caching adds storage / invalidation complexity for multi-device sessions. Need clear TTL policy (suggest 45s sliding TTL for live captions).
- Edge-case: long transcripts occasionally require the 70b model for context-aware disambiguation; maintain fallback route (auto-escape) when summarizer confidence < threshold.

Open questions for LM + next steps:
- LM product: confirm acceptable ROUGE/WER thresholds and whether human review pipeline can be used during canary.
- LM infra: can they expose per-session identifiers in requests to enable proper KV reuse? If not, caching benefit reduces ~60%.
- Finance: determine billing model for hybrid routing during canary (split metering vs blended invoice).

Appendix - quick calcs (rounded):
- Baseline cost per 1M tokens: $371.4 (derived from $15,600 / 42M * 1M).
- Central scenario cost per 1M tokens after Optimize bundle: $154.8.
- Primary levers: routing (short-turn), quantization, batching, caching, response caps.

- [Mateo] provision warm pool and instrument p95 telemetry; infra PR posted.

This doc is a working quickscan — numbers are intentionally conservative in some places and optimistic in others. Recommend follow-up offline eval before presenting a formal savings guarantee.
